topic: Link parsing, private servers and share links (RoALT), verified 2026-10-24

findings.claim: The share-link resolver is POST https://apis.roblox.com/sharelinks/v1/resolve-link with body {"linkId":<code>,"linkType":<type>}. It needs a CSRF token, and every game-relevant type needs a logged-in cookie.
findings.detail:
Observed with curl, no cookie sent.
(a) Without x-csrf-token the call returns 403 with body {"errors":[{"code":0,"message":"XSRF token invalid"}]}. The response carries an x-csrf-token header and access-control-expose-headers: x-csrf-token.
(b) With the token but no cookie it returns 401. The body is a bare JSON string, not the usual {errors:[]} envelope: "User must be authenticated to use 'Server' links". The same 401 comes back for ExperienceDetails, ExperienceInvite, FriendInvite, NotificationExperienceInvite, Profile, ScreenshotInvite, AvatarItemDetails, ContentPost and ExperienceEvent.
(c) ExperienceAffiliate returns 200 without a cookie: {experienceInviteData:null, …, experienceAffiliateData:{status:"Invalid"}, experienceEventData:null}.
(d) An unknown type returns 404 "unhandled link type 'Bogus'". PrivateServer and Screenshot are also unknown.
(e) A missing linkId returns 400 "Error while resolving the link."
(f) linkType is parsed case-insensitively ("server" maps to 'Server') and also accepts JSON numbers: 0 Invalid, 1 ExperienceInvite, 2 FriendInvite, 3 NotificationExperienceInvite, 4 Profile, 5 ScreenshotInvite, 6 Server, 7 ExperienceDetails, 8 AvatarItemDetails, 9 ContentPost, 10 ExperienceAffiliate, 11 ExperienceEvent. Value 12 is unnamed and returns avatarItemDetailsData without auth.
The 401 response headers include x-ratelimit-limit: 10000, 10000;w=60.
There is no swagger: /sharelinks/docs/json/v1 and the other docs paths all return 404.

findings.claim: Roblox's own web client reads only status, universeId and linkCode from privateServerInviteData. It then turns universeId into the root place ID itself. There is no evidence of placeId, ownerUserId, privateServerId or expiration fields.
findings.detail:
This comes from the DeepLinkService code in CoreUtilities.js, in the `case w3.SERVER` branch. It reads r = t.data.privateServerInviteData and checks r.universeId != null and r.status in [Valid, Expired]. It then calls getPlaceIdFromUniverseId(universeId), which is GET https://games.roblox.com/v1/games?universeIds=<id> reading data[0].rootPlaceId. Finally it sets window.location.href = '/games/' + rootPlaceId + '?privateServerLinkCode=' + r.linkCode.
The status enum for the Server type (named PrivateServerLinkStatus in the code) is Invalid | Valid | Expired. The web proceeds on Expired as well as Valid.
The full v1 response envelope, observed live, has 11 keys: experienceInviteData, friendInviteData, notificationExperienceInviteData, profileLinkResolutionResponseData, screenshotInviteData, privateServerInviteData, experienceDetailsInviteData, avatarItemDetailsData, contentPostData, experienceAffiliateData, experienceEventData.
The JSON type of linkCode is unconfirmed; the web concatenates it into a string. Other fields in privateServerInviteData may exist but are unconfirmed, because no authenticated capture was made.
A community fork (pealz1/RobloxAccountManager, roblox_api.py) regex-searches the response for "placeId". That contradicts Roblox's own consumer and is likely broken.

findings.claim: The official web flow for a type=Server share link is: /share, then an AppsFlyer redirect, then /share-links, then resolve-link, then /games/{rootPlaceId}?privateServerLinkCode={linkCode}, then RequestPrivateGame with placeId and linkCode. accessCode is sent empty.
findings.detail:
1. GET https://www.roblox.com/share?code=ce65b2c80e8dae48866fe2f919966557&type=Server returns 302 to https://ro.blox.com/Ebh5?pid=Server&is_retargeting=false&af_dp=<enc roblox://navigation/share_links?code=..&type=Server>&deep_link_value=<same>&af_web_dp=<enc https://www.roblox.com/share-links?code=..&type=Server>.
2. /share-links returns 200 and renders <div id="share-links-container" data-link-id data-link-type data-link-version data-instance-id data-annotation-id>.
3. ShareLinks.js resolves only if authenticatedUser.isAuthenticated, or if the type is ExperienceAffiliate or AvatarItemAffiliate. Otherwise it redirects to /login?returnUrl=.
4. ShareLinks.js calls DeepLinkService.navigateToDeepLink('roblox://navigation/share_links?code=X&type=T'), which resolves as in L2.
5. The game page Play button calls joinPrivateGame(placeId, null, linkCode). GameLaunch.js builds placelauncherurl = https://www.roblox.com/Game/PlaceLauncher.ashx?request=RequestPrivateGame&browserTrackerId=..&placeId=..&accessCode=&linkCode=..[&joinAttemptId=<uuid>&joinAttemptOrigin=..].
Related: the old approach of scraping the inline Roblox.GameLauncher.joinPrivateGame(placeId,'<accessCode GUID>','<linkCode>') from the game page, as Roblox-Account-Manager master does in Account.cs, is dead. The current game HTML has 0 occurrences of joinPrivateGame. A fork's open issue says the same (ethanstoner/Roblox-Account-Manager #14, 2026-09-23).

findings.claim: Joining via a share link needs no separate 'accept' API call. The only extra step is the logged-in resolve-link call, which the joining account itself makes. It is unverified whether RequestPrivateGame with a linkCode works for an account that never called resolve.
findings.detail:
In the web code, nothing happens between resolve and the redirect to /games/{rootPlaceId}?privateServerLinkCode= except analytics (sendEvent 'linkResolved'). The play path then calls RequestPrivateGame with linkCode only.
The classic privateServerLinkCode links (2023 and earlier) worked for any account holding the code. Roblox staff said in Oct 2023: 'we're still using the Private Server Link Code and Game ID under the hood'. That post may be stale.
Unknown: whether resolve-link has a server-side side effect such as registering the user. Every web join resolves with the joiner's own cookie, so mirroring that is the safe default.
The recipient's own settings may still block the join. Community sources describe the 'who can invite me to private servers' privacy setting and under-13 accounts limited to friends' servers (error 524). Roblox-Account-Manager historically checked www.roblox.com/account/settings/private-server-invite-privacy for 'AllUsers'. That endpoint was reported removed (ethanstoner #11, 2026-09-23), with the setting moved to apis.roblox.com/user-settings-api/v1/user-settings; the key name is unconfirmed.
The owner-side endpoint GET https://games.roblox.com/v1/vip-server/can-invite/{userId} returns {canInvite, doesOwnerPrivacyRestrictJoins, inviteResponseType}.

findings.claim: There is a second share-link format, v2: /share?code=X&v=v2 with no type. It resolves via POST https://apis.roblox.com/deeplinks/v2/resolve with body {linkId}.
findings.detail:
GET https://www.roblox.com/share?code=abc123&v=v2 returns 302 to https://ro.blox.com/Ebh5?pid=sharelinkv2&is_retargeting=false&af_dp=<enc roblox://navigation/share_links?code=abc123&v=v2>&af_web_dp=<enc https://www.roblox.com/share-links?code=abc123&v=v2>&af_force_deeplink=true.
In the env config, shareLinksApiV2 = 'https://apis.'+domain+'/deeplinks' and the path is '/v2/resolve'.
Without a cookie it returns 401 {"errors":[{"code":9002,"subcode":0,"message":"Authentication token is missing"}]}.
The web reads data.linkType, data.status, data.targetId and data.customData. linkType values are Experience, StudioEdit, StudioTeamTest, UserTrustedConnection, StudioTrustedConnection, Moments, SchoolInvite and Referral. For Experience, targetId is a placeId and customData becomes launchData (default '{}'). The share-links page may also carry instanceId and annotationId, which are used only for Studio links.
The character set of v2 codes is unknown.

findings.claim: Several other share-link types can be turned into a launch target after resolving. The web client knows 12 types.
sources: CoreUtilities.js (switch on share type in DeepLinkService), captured 2026-10-24

findings.claim: Classic privateServerLinkCode values are digits only and not fixed length: 32 digits is typical, but 25-digit codes occur. Share codes for typed links are 32 lowercase hex characters. Keep both as strings.
findings.detail:
Real examples:
- https://www.roblox.com/games/76558904092080?privateServerLinkCode=58201880850229913874098176522742 (32 digits; techwiser, Jan 2026)
- https://www.roblox.com/games/90906407195271/Racket-Rivals?privateServerLinkCode=1020499390872690887970171 (25 digits; pyrobloxbot docs, the result of following a share link)
RoSeal's Roblox-DeepLink-Parser validates privateServerLinkCode and linkCode with ^\d+$. Note the place IDs above are 14 digits (beyond 2^32), so use u64/i64.
Share code examples: ce65b2c80e8dae48866fe2f919966557 (DevForum, Feb 2025) and 864059867507234896ed98bd1b78a8dc (pyrobloxbot).
Regenerating a server's invite link changes the link code (pyrobloxbot; community).
Legacy note: the DevForum OP of Feb 2025 wrote privateServerLink={[0-9]{32}}.

findings.claim: How the live site treats game URL variants: www, apex and web.roblox.com all canonicalise to www; m.roblox.com is gone; the slug is ignored; the path is case-insensitive; the query survives redirects; a locale prefix is accepted.
findings.detail:
Unauthenticated GETs, 2026-10-24:
- /games/920587237 returns 301 to /games/920587237/Adopt-Me. So do /games/920587237/ and /games/920587237/Wrong-Slug.
- /games/920587237?privateServerLinkCode=123 returns 301 to /games/920587237/Adopt-Me?privateServerLinkCode=123.
- https://roblox.com/... returns 308 to www. https://web.roblox.com/... returns 302 to https://www.roblox.com:443/...
- https://m.roblox.com/games/920587237 returns 404.
- /de/games/.. returns 200. /pt-br/games/.. returns 302 to /pt/games/.. ; /zh-cn/games/.. returns 302 to /games/..
- /GAMES/920587237/Adopt-Me returns 200.
- /games/0/x returns 302 to /request-error?code=404.
- /experiences/920587237 returns 404, as does /games/refer?PlaceId=..
- /share?type=Server with no code returns 404.
RateLimit on /share is 10 per 60 s.
RoSeal's locale regex is /^[a-z]{2}(-[a-z0-9]{2,3})?$/i, excluding 'js' and 'my'.

findings.claim: Official launch parameters are placeId, userId, accessCode, linkCode, gameInstanceId and launchData. Roblox documents the web and app deep-link forms, and marks the deep-link page deprecated in favour of share links.
findings.detail:
create.roblox.com/docs/production/promotion/deeplinking documents:
- https://www.roblox.com/games/start?placeId=<id>&launchData=<string>
- roblox://placeId=<id>&launchData=<string>
- ro.blox.com/Ebh5?af_dp=<enc app link>&af_web_dp=<enc web link>
Parameters: placeId (required unless userId), userId (follow; error 'Followed user has left the game'), accessCode (private server access code), linkCode (private server link code), gameInstanceId (= DataModel.JobId), launchData (decoded size must be ≤ 200 bytes, read in game via Player:GetJoinData().LaunchData).
Observed: without a cookie, /games/start renders the game page with an inline redirect, Roblox.PrivateServerLinkJoin.init(function(){window.location.href='roblox://experiences/start?placeId=920587237&launchData=abc'}). That redirect dropped gameInstanceId, linkCode and privateServerLinkCode. Behaviour with a logged-in cookie is unknown.

findings.claim: roblox:// deep links come in three forms: the legacy roblox://placeId=..&.., the current roblox://experiences/start?.., and roblox://navigation/<route>?... They act on whichever account the Roblox app itself is logged into.
findings.detail:
Roblox web constants (CoreUtilities.js): ExperienceLauncher = "roblox://experiences/start?" and AppLauncher = "roblox://navigation".
The web deep-link parser splits with path regex /\/(\w+)/g and param regex /(\w+)=([^&=]+)/g. Its handlers are keyed by the first path word:
- navigation: share_links, game_details?gameId=<universeId>, profile?userId=, and others
- placeId (legacy roblox://placeId=..): if linkCode, go to /games/{placeId}?privateServerLinkCode={linkCode}; else if accessCode, go to /games/start?placeId=&accessCode=; else if launchData, go to roblox://experiences/start?placeId=&launchData=; else joinMultiplayerGame
- userId: go to /games/start?userId=
- group
Bloxstrap's ActivityData.GetInviteDeeplink builds roblox://experiences/start?placeId={PlaceId} plus &accessCode={AccessCode} for private servers, otherwise &gameInstanceId={JobId}, plus optional &launchData=.
BTRoblox's README gives the examples roblox://experiences/start?id=1818 and roblox://placeId=1818/. Its param list: placeId (alias id), gameInstanceId, accessCode, linkCode, launchData, reservedServerAccessCode, joinAttemptId, joinAttemptOrigin, callId, browserTrackerId.
RoSeal's parser adds referralPage, referredByPlayerId, eventId and isoContext. It matches query keys case-insensitively and treats a legacy path containing '=' with no '?' as the query string.
Also seen: roblox://navigation/share_links?code=..&type=Server (DevForum, Feb 2025) and roblox://navigation/share_links?code=..&v=v2.

findings.claim: ro.blox.com/Ebh5 is an AppsFlyer OneLink wrapper. The real target sits in af_dp, then deep_link_value, then af_web_dp.
findings.detail:
RoSeal's default AppsFlyer base is "ro.blox.com/Ebh5". It reads af_dp first, falls back to deep_link_value (both are roblox:// links), and uses af_web_dp (an https www link) only if neither is present.
The Roblox web client itself opens https://ro.blox.com/Ebh5?<query>&af_dp=<s>&af_web_dp=<s>&deep_link_value=<s> on mobile and ChromeOS.
Short forms with no query (ro.blox.com/Ebh5/<id>) can only be resolved by contacting AppsFlyer, which is not a Roblox host.

findings.claim: A job ID (gameInstanceId) is a lowercase version-4 GUID. You join one with RequestGameJob&placeId=..&gameId=<jobId>.
findings.detail:
GET https://games.roblox.com/v1/games/920587237/servers/Public?limit=10&sortOrder=Desc returns ids such as c63bf72f-b8d0-4675-8d80-887388c603a3, alongside fields fps, id, maxPlayers, ping, playerTokens, players and playing. Without a cookie that endpoint has x-ratelimit-limit: 3, 3;w=60.
Where users get job IDs: server lists on the site, RoPro and BTRoblox; the in-game developer console (game.JobId); Bloxstrap's copied invite link (roblox://experiences/start?placeId=&gameInstanceId=); and presence gameId, but only when the target's privacy lets the caller see it.
Web GameLaunch: joinGameInstance builds placelauncherurl request=RequestGameJob with placeId and gameId (plus isPlayTogetherGame and optional referredByPlayerId).
The pyrobloxbot docs give an underscore-style example, D01F4F55_045B_4727_9A19_E694027D3F8A_69AA65738_2657. The live API contradicts it, so treat it as wrong or stale.

findings.claim: 'Join user' is RequestFollowUser&userId=<id>. It only works while the target is in a game and the target's own 'who can join me' privacy allows the joining account. That setting cannot be read for other users.
findings.detail:
Web GameLaunch: followPlayerIntoGame({userId}) builds placelauncherurl https://www.roblox.com/Game/PlaceLauncher.ashx?request=RequestFollowUser&browserTrackerId=..&userId=..[&joinAttemptId&joinAttemptOrigin].
Deep-link equivalents: roblox://userId=<id> (the web maps it to /games/start?userId=) and roblox://experiences/start?userId=<id> (RoSeal's joinUser).
Presence: POST https://presence.roblox.com/v1/presence/users with {"userIds":[..]} returns userPresenceType (0 Offline, 1 Website, 2 InGame, 3 Studio), lastLocation, placeId, rootPlaceId, gameId, universeId and userId. Those IDs are null when hidden from the caller, as in the unauthenticated capture.
Privacy: no API reads another user's setting (DevForum, Apr 2023, possibly stale). The old self endpoint www.roblox.com/account/settings/follow-me-privacy was reported removed, replaced by apis.roblox.com/user-settings-api/v1/user-settings. That endpoint returns 401 'Authentication token is missing' without a cookie, and its key name and enum values are unconfirmed.
Option names in community guides vary (Everyone / Friends / No one, plus variants with 'users I follow'), so they are unconfirmed. Friendship is not strictly required when the target allows Everyone (community, inferred).

findings.claim: A second private-server path exists: the accessCode, a GUID. An account that already has access can fetch it without any link.
findings.detail:
GET https://games.roblox.com/v1/games/{placeId}/private-servers (marked EXPERIMENTAL) returns data[] items with fields id, maxPlayers, playing, playerTokens, players, fps, ping, name, vipServerId, accessCode, owner, plus gameJoinRestricted and the paging cursors.
The owner's PATCH /v1/vip-servers/{id} returns PrivateServerResponse {id, name, game, joinCode, active, subscription, permissions, link}.
With an accessCode, RequestPrivateGame&placeId&accessCode=<guid> works; Bloxstrap shares accessCode deep links. reservedServerAccessCode, the code from TeleportService reserved servers, is a separate parameter.

findings.claim: The legacy swagger URLs (https://<svc>.roblox.com/docs/json/v1) now redirect to a trimmed copy on prod.docsiteassets.roblox.com. sharelinks, deeplinks and gamejoin have no public swagger.
findings.detail:
friends.roblox.com/docs/json/v1 returns 302 to https://prod.docsiteassets.roblox.com/assets/en-us/cloud/legacy/friends/v1.json. The same pattern works for games and accountsettings.
The games v1 copy lists only 9 paths and omits the servers and private-server endpoints, so use create.roblox.com/docs/cloud/reference/features/*.md for those.
games.roblox.com/docs/json/v1 returns 404. gamejoin's docsiteassets copy returns 403.

findings.claim: Parsing rules for RoALT, precise enough to write unit tests. A reference implementation passes all 38 cases.
findings.detail:
Inputs are tried in this order.
R0 Input cleanup and bare values:
- Trim whitespace and surrounding <>'".
- An empty string is Invalid(empty).
- Bare digits matching ^[0-9]{1,19}$ with 0 < n ≤ 2^63-1 give Place{placeId}.
- A bare UUID (case-insensitive) gives JobIdOnly{jobId}, lowercased; the UI must then ask for a place.
R1 Scheme:
- roblox:// (scheme case-insensitive) goes to R5.
- roblox-player:, roblox-studio: and roblox-studio-auth: are Invalid, because these URIs carry an auth ticket.
- If there is no scheme, prepend https://.
- Any scheme other than http/https is Invalid.
R2 Host (lowercased, trailing dot stripped, port ignored):
- ro.blox.com goes to R6.
- The host must be exactly one of roblox.com, www.roblox.com, web.roblox.com or m.roblox.com. No other subdomain is allowed (create.roblox.com is Invalid), and suffix or lookalike hosts are Invalid.
R3 Path:
- Split on '/' and drop empty segments.
- If seg[0] matches /^[a-z]{2}(-[a-z0-9]{2,4})?$/i and seg[1] (case-insensitive) is games, share, share-links or users, drop seg[0].
- Compare segment names case-insensitively.
- Query keys are case-insensitive; the first occurrence wins. Values are URL-decoded once. Ignore the fragment.
R4 Routes:
(a) /games/start: apply rule Q.
(b) /games/{id}[/{slug}...]: id must be a valid ID, else Invalid(placeId). Then:
- privateServerLinkCode present: it must match ^[0-9]{1,64}$, giving PrivateServerLinkCode{placeId, linkCode as string}; otherwise Invalid(linkCode).
- else gameInstanceId present: it must be a UUID, giving Instance{placeId, jobId}; otherwise Invalid(jobId).
- else Place{placeId}.
(c) /share or /share-links: apply rule S.
(d) /users/{id}[/profile]: User{userId}.
(e) Anything else: Unsupported(not a game link).
Rule Q (shared by /games/start and the roblox:// launch forms):
- placeId (alias id) absent: if userId is present, FollowUser{userId}; else Invalid(placeId).
- else if linkCode or privateServerLinkCode is present: it must be digits, giving PrivateServerLinkCode.
- else if accessCode is present: it must be a UUID, giving PrivateServerAccessCode.
- else if gameInstanceId is present: it must be a UUID, giving Instance.
- else Place{placeId, launchData if non-empty}.
This precedence mirrors the web's Sm and SW functions.
Rule S:
- code must be present and match ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}$, else Invalid.
- v=v2 gives ShareLinkV2{code}.
- type missing gives Invalid(share type missing).
- Match type case-insensitively against the 12 known types; an unknown type is Invalid.
- FriendInvite, AvatarItemDetails, AvatarItemAffiliate and ContentPost give Unsupported(not a game link).
- Otherwise ShareLink{code, linkType canonical-cased}.
R5 roblox://<rest>:
- Split rest at the first '?'. If there is no '?' and the path contains '=', treat the path (trailing '/' stripped) as the query, with an empty path.
- An empty path or experiences/start applies Q.
- navigation/share_links applies S.
- navigation/game_details?gameId=<n> gives Universe{universeId}; this needs a lookup via games.roblox.com/v1/games?universeIds= and data[0].rootPlaceId.
- navigation/profile?userId= gives User.
- Any other route is Unsupported.
R6 ro.blox.com:
- Take the first non-empty of af_dp, deep_link_value, af_web_dp and re-parse it at depth+1. A nested ro.blox.com link is Invalid.
- If none is present, Unsupported (short link); never fetch it.
Cases (input → expected; the full list is in links-parse-cases.json):
1. https://www.roblox.com/games/920587237/Adopt-Me → Place 920587237
2. roblox.com/games/920587237 → Place
3. <https://www.roblox.com/de/games/920587237/Adopt-Me#!/game-instances> → Place
4. https://web.roblox.com/games/76558904092080?privateServerLinkCode=58201880850229913874098176522742 → PrivateServerLinkCode{76558904092080, "5820…742"}
5. …/games/90906407195271/Racket-Rivals?privateServerLinkCode=1020499390872690887970171 → PrivateServerLinkCode (25 digits)
6. https://www.roblox.com/share?code=ce65b2c80e8dae48866fe2f919966557&type=Server → ShareLink Server
7. /share-links?code=..&type=server → ShareLink Server
8. the captured ro.blox.com/Ebh5?pid=Server&af_dp=… → ShareLink Server
9. roblox://navigation/share_links?code=..&type=ExperienceInvite → ShareLink ExperienceInvite
10. /share?code=abc123&v=v2 → ShareLinkV2
11. roblox://placeId=920587237&launchData=abc%20def → Place + launchData 'abc def'
12. roblox://placeId=1818/ → Place 1818
13. roblox://experiences/start?placeId=920587237&gameInstanceId=C63BF72F-… → Instance, jobId lowercased
14. roblox://experiences/start?id=1818 → Place
15. roblox://experiences/start?placeId=..&accessCode=<guid> → PrivateServerAccessCode
16. roblox://placeId=920587237&linkCode=5820… → PrivateServerLinkCode
17. /games/start?placeId=920587237&launchData=%7B%22a%22%3A1%7D → Place + launchData {"a":1}
18. roblox://userId=156 → FollowUser 156
19. /games/start?userId=156 → FollowUser
20. /users/156/profile → User 156
21. roblox://navigation/game_details?gameId=383310974 → Universe (root place 920587237)
22. 920587237 → Place
23. c63bf72f-b8d0-4675-8d80-887388c603a3 → JobIdOnly
Invalid or unsupported cases:
- https://www.roblox.com.evil.example/games/1/x → Invalid(host). So are evilroblox.com and create.roblox.com/docs.
- /games/abc/x, /games/0/x and /games/99999999999999999999/x → Invalid(placeId)
- privateServerLinkCode=12ab → Invalid(linkCode)
- gameInstanceId=not-a-guid → Invalid(jobId)
- /share?code=.. with no type → Invalid
- type=FriendInvite → Unsupported
- /catalog/1365767/.. → Unsupported
- ro.blox.com/Ebh5/a1b2c3 → Unsupported
- roblox-player:1+launchmode:play+… → Invalid
- "" → Invalid

open_questions: Does RequestPrivateGame with only placeId and linkCode succeed for an account that never called resolve-link or opened the share link? The web code shows no accept step, but this needs a real-account test.

What is the full privateServerInviteData schema with a logged-in cookie? Is linkCode a string or a number? Are there fields such as expiration, owner or privateServerId? Only status, universeId and linkCode are confirmed.
Does a link whose status is Expired still join? The web proceeds on Expired the same as Valid.

Does the recipient's 'who can invite me to private servers' privacy setting, or an under-13 account, block joins by link code? What is the key name and what are the values in apis.roblox.com/user-settings-api/v1/user-settings for that setting and for 'who can join me'?
With a logged-in cookie, does /games/start keep gameInstanceId, linkCode or accessCode in its inline roblox://experiences/start redirect? Without a cookie it drops them.
What character set and length do v2 share codes (v=v2) use? Which v2 linkTypes appear for game invites in practice?
What does the roblox://navigation/share_links/{type}/{code} static form (RoSeal) look like in the wild? Its type group matches a single \w character, which may be a RoSeal bug.
Is the unauthenticated rate limit of 3 requests per 60 s on games.roblox.com/v1/games/{placeId}/servers/Public higher with a cookie?
design_implications: Parse locally with the R0–R6 rules in L16. A reference implementation that passes all 38 cases is at <scratchpad>/scripts\ref_parse.py; port it to Rust and reuse the cases file as test fixtures.

Use a tagged enum for the target: Place{placeId, launchData?}, Instance{placeId, jobId}, PrivateServerLinkCode{placeId, linkCode:String}, PrivateServerAccessCode{placeId, accessCode}, ShareLink{code, linkType}, ShareLinkV2{code}, Universe{universeId}, FollowUser{userId}, User{userId}, JobIdOnly{jobId}, Invalid{reason}, Unsupported{reason}. IDs are u64 ≤ i64::MAX. Keep linkCode and share codes as strings, never numbers.

Resolve share links per account, inside the launch pipeline, with that account's own cookie. Mirror the web: POST sharelinks/v1/resolve-link, retry once on 403 with the x-csrf-token from the response, and handle a 401 whose body is a bare JSON string. For type=Server, read privateServerInviteData.status, universeId and linkCode, map universeId to rootPlaceId via games.roblox.com/v1/games?universeIds=, then launch RequestPrivateGame with placeId=rootPlaceId and linkCode (accessCode empty). In bulk launch, resolve once per account rather than reusing another account's result until L4 is verified.

Treat status Invalid as a user-facing error and let Expired proceed with a warning, as the web does. Map ExperienceInvite with Valid status plus instanceId to Instance. Map ExperienceDetails, ExperienceAffiliate and ExperienceEvent to a Place via universeId and rootPlaceId, passing joinData.launchData. Map v2 Experience to Place(targetId, launchData=customData).
